decision.explanation: The central register excerpt, issued on 2027-09-14 and current on the decision date, identifies Dormun Pefenka as the 100% beneficial owner, whereas the customer's declaration identifies Relpe Petorvi as the 100% beneficial owner. The internal record shows standard risk and no alerts but does not identify the beneficial owners. No tier 1 or 2 source other than the register establishes beneficial ownership; the customer's tier 3 declaration cannot establish a reportable discrepancy or justify treating the register as merely outdated. Under R2, request a tier 1 or 2 document identifying the current beneficial owners, such as an official shareholder excerpt or notarial deed, before determining the discrepancy action.

The central register and the tier 1 business-register shareholder excerpt both identify Dormun Pefenka (born 1994-06-15) as the 100% owner, so the reliable evidence does not establish a register discrepancy. Both excerpts were issued within 30 days of the decision date. However, the customer's declaration identifies Relpe Petorvi (born 1951-02-04) as the 100% beneficial owner, contradicting the reliable evidence. Under R2, request clarification and supporting documentation reconciling that declaration with the official ownership records before finalising the determination. The internal record shows standard risk and no alerts; there is no documented concealment alert requiring escalation.

The current central register entry identifies Dormun Pefenka as the 100% beneficial owner, whereas the current tier 1 business-register shareholder excerpt identifies Relpe Petorvi as the 100% shareholder since 2024-10-17. This establishes a substantive ownership discrepancy under R2, not a typographical or transliteration error. Although the customer is standard-risk and has no recorded alerts, the evidence does not establish that the register is merely outdated or that the business register is independent of the central register's controlling authority, so exception (b) is not available. Report the discrepancy to the central register within 14 calendar days of the decision date, by 2027-09-30.

Report the discrepancy to the central register within 14 calendar days under R2. Although the customer is standard-risk and has no recorded alerts, the evidence does not establish that the register is merely outdated or that the business register is independent of the central register's controlling authority, so the customer-correction exception is not available. Independence is not required to establish the discrepancy itself.
